newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says Iran supporting Egyptian militants.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Iran supporting Egyptian militants.

text.p: Egyptian Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi said Iran and Sudan continued to support the militant Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the largest organisation fighting to overthrow the Egyptian government.
In a statement to the consultative chamber of parliament on Sunday, Alfi said Iranian support was channelled through an Iranian embassy outside Egypt.

"It has been discovered that Iran is involved in a conspiratorial role directed against Egypt through one of the Iranian embassies abroad to support the organisation (the Gama'a) and its members," he said. The minister was quoted in government newspapers on Monday.

"There is also the Iranian presence in Sudan, with the Sudanese regime...continuing to embrace and shelter its (Gama'a) leaders and members and to provide material, moral support and constant training," he added.
The newspapers gave no further details of Iranian support for the Gama'a, which has been fighting since 1992 to turn Egypt into a strict Islamic state.
Egypt has sporadically said Iran supports the Gama'a. President Hosni Mubarak said last year that Iran helped in the Gama'a attempt to assassinate him in Addis Ababa in 1995.
In January one of Mubarak's senior aides, Osama el-Baz, said Iran was using Sudan as a "Trojan house" to infiltrate Africa.
